newsitem.title: USA: Senators urge EPA not to tighten air standards.
newsitem.headline: Senators urge EPA not to tighten air standards.

text.p: Five coal state senators have urged the Clinton administration to stick with current clean air standards instead of tightening them as proposed by the Environmental Protection Agency.

"Because of the significant uncertainty surrounding the costs, benefits and impacts of EPA's proposed ozone and PM (particulate matter) rules, we urge the EPA to reaffirm the current standards," the senators said in a March 4 letter to EPA Administrator Carol Browner released Thursday.
Coal-fired power could be heavily affected by the EPA's controversial proposal to set stricter limits on soot and smog-forming ozone.
The agency is under a court-ordered deadline to issue a final clean air rule in July.
Its proposal has sparked vehement opposition among industry groups, states and local communities which are concerned that the new standards will cost billions of dollars.
But health advocates say tighter standards will protect thousands of lives, especially those of asthmatic children.

The senators, led by the top Democrat on the Senate Appropriations Committee, Robert Byrd of West Virginia, said instead of setting new limits, the EPA should do more studies and "allow our states to complete action on the ambitious clean air standards that are already in place."
The letter was also signed by Democratic Sens. Jay Rockefeller of West Virginia, Chuck Robb of Virginia, John Glenn of Ohio and Wendell Ford of Kentucky.
Some Senate Republicans, including Senate Environment Committee Chairman John Chafee of Rhode Island, have also raised concerns about the proposal.
